segs.text: ClipFund: an AI agent that earns its own stock treasury, on Base.
My entry for Base Stocks Maxxing · Track 2.1
Clipping streams is repetitive work, a good fit for an agent.
But agent treasuries are usually a black box, and one key can spend everything.
ClipFund sells clips for $0.50 USDC over x402, paid straight into a treasury contract.
Reserve first (locked). Then an owner-set share of the surplus buys tokenized stocks. The rest stays as USDC.
The rules live in one contract. All 13 Foundry tests pass, including a 512-run fuzz test.
Live demo on a local fork of Base Sepolia (chain 84532).
POST /clip without paying → HTTP 402 Payment Required: 0.50 USDC to the treasury.
Client signs an EIP-3009 USDC authorization → HTTP 200 + clip → settled onchain → recordPayment().
Payments 1–2 go 100% to the locked reserve until it hits its $1.00 target.
Then 60% of surplus → stock budget → the agent buys sCOIN and sNVDA.
Each stock is capped at 35% of treasury NAV. Above the cap, the buy reverts.
Operating costs come from the reserve only, to an allowlisted payee. The next payment refills it first.
Rebuilt from onchain events: all 12 reconciliation checks pass, every payment matched to its x402 settlement tx.
What the customer paid for: a 9:16 headline clip, cut with ffmpeg.
The agent key can't change policy or withdraw. The reserve can't be invested. Payments can't be faked or booked twice.
To be clear: testnet demo, local Base Sepolia fork, test USDC, no real money.
sCOIN / sNVDA are simulated test tokens (fixed mock price, no rights in any company). The x402 facilitator runs in-process.
Useful work → revenue → reserve → stock treasury.
